name: Naturalización

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 consecutive years of residence, having reached the age of majority, a declaration of intent to naturalise, renunciation of prior nationality, and proof of Spanish-language competency plus basic knowledge of Panamanian geography, history, and political organisation.
requirements.fix_path: Accrue 5 consecutive years of residence and pass the language/civics assessment.

requirement_groups.name: Reduced track (Constitution Article 10.2): married to a Panamanian, or has children born in Panama to Panamanian parents

requirements.blocker_text: Requires only 3 consecutive years of residence for those married to a Panamanian national, or who have children born in Panama to Panamanian parents -- same age, declaration, renunciation, and language/civics requirements as the ordinary track otherwise apply.
requirements.fix_path: Accrue 3 consecutive years of residence while in a qualifying category, and pass the language/civics assessment.

requirement_groups.name: Privileged track (Constitution Article 10.3): Spanish nationals or Latin-American-born applicants

requirements.blocker_text: Spanish nationals, or those born in a Latin American country, may naturalise under whatever conditions that country itself requires for Panamanian nationals to naturalise there (a reciprocity principle) -- the Constitution does not specify a fixed residence term for this track, and the exact reciprocal terms vary by country and were not individually researched in this pass.

evidence_required.document: Power of attorney and formal application addressed to the President of the Republic
Permanent Resident Card, authenticated by the Electoral Tribunal
Medical certificate of good health (90-day validity)
Economic solvency proof (two of: tax returns, bank letter, employment letter with Social Security records, investment/property proof)
Spanish language and Panamanian geography/history/civics assessment

sources.title: Tribunal Electoral de Panamá -- Constitución Política, Título II, Artículo 10: three naturalisation tracks (5yr ordinary, 3yr reduced, privileged reciprocity)
Servicio Nacional de Migración de Panamá -- Requisitos de Naturalización 2024: full document checklist (does not itself restate the residence-year figures, which come from the Constitution)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Panama's initial build. STATUS SET TO DRAFT despite tier-1 sourcing on both the Constitution and the document checklist: the Constitution's own text explicitly requires RENUNCIATION of prior nationality for naturalisation (dual_citizenship_allowed set false for this route specifically) -- yet Panama is widely described elsewhere as permitting dual nationality for those who acquire it by OTHER means (e.g. by descent, see pa_citizenship_descent, which does allow dual nationality) and even reportedly in practice for some naturalised citizens; this apparent tension between the literal constitutional renunciation requirement and common real-world reporting was not reconciled in this pass, so the route is held at draft rather than asserting either version confidently. THREE GENUINELY DIFFERENT TRACKS modelled as OR-logic groups since the Constitution itself presents them as one naturalisation process (Article 10, numerals 1-3) with alternative grounds. The privileged reciprocity track's actual terms depend on the applicant's specific country of origin/citizenship and were not researched country-by-country.
